model: Diversified conglomerate: Underlying Net Profit capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route; property IP/DP + hotels + logistics + wind-down investment portfolio)
model_label: Underlying Net Profit (management's audited non-GAAP measure, ex IP revaluation and MTM) discounted at cost of equity, component-built; hybrid of the REIT/distributable-profit row (fair-value noise stripped, capitalise post-financing flow at CoE) and the holdco/BVPS-compounding row (mixed DP/hotels/logistics operating businesses, net-cash balance sheet)

equity_bridge.item: Net cash, 31 Dec 2025 (FY2025 balance sheet: HK$19,868m bank deposits/cash less HK$17,906m debt)
equity_bridge.note: FY2025 Annual Report Financial Highlights, p.5. Not double counted: net_debt is held at zero in the flow (see net_debt_note) because UNP is already post-interest.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Revenue CAGRs are deeply negative (-22.1% 3yr, -13.5% 5yr) while EPS/UNP CAGRs are positive -- an extreme divergence, but not a data-quality flag: it is explained structurally (deliberate Mainland DP land-bank wind-down since 2019 plus progressive investment-portfolio realisation shrinking revenue while UNP, the distributable measure, holds up). Statutory EPS 3yr CAGR (42.2%) is distorted by the FY2022 near-zero base (EPS HK$-0.56) and is not used; fcf_*_cagr are left null because reported FCF (a mix of DP inventory-cycle OCF, portfolio disposal proceeds routed through investing activities, and swings from HK$-10,595m FY2018 to +HK$8,981m FY2020) has no stable trend and UNP is used as the owner flow directly instead (dcf-methods SKILL.md REIT-row rule: use the distribution/underlying series, not reported cash flow, when fair-value noise dominates statutory numbers). Selected growth rate is UNP's own 5yr CAGR (3.0%), used only as the long-run anchor the path fades toward -- the near-term path is built bottom-up from disclosed H1-2026 segment trends, not by applying this CAGR mechanically.
historical_growth.notes: Book NAV/share fell at a -2.4% 5yr CAGR (HK$53.02 FY2021 -> HK$48.01 FY2025) despite positive cumulative UNP over the period, because dividends (flat HK$0.40/share, ~30% of a rising UNP in most years) plus periodic statutory losses (largely non-cash revaluation) have outpaced retained UNP; this corroborates treating 0004.HK as a mature, low-growth, capital-return name rather than a compounder.

scenario_narratives.base: The disclosed H1-2026 step-down in Investments segment profit (-41% YoY as the ~HK$40bn portfolio continues to be progressively realised) pulls Group UNP below the FY2025 peak of HK$4,104m for one to two years, before the drag fades: the Mainland DP legacy book keeps shrinking its impairment charge (loss narrowed 75% in FY2025 alone), IP holds roughly flat on continued luxury-brand demand at Chengdu/Changsha even as Mainland retail stays soft, and Logistics is roughly stable as DaChan Bay growth partly offsets Hong Kong throughput decline. UNP settles into low-single-digit growth, reflecting a mature, capital-return conglomerate (NAV/share CAGR has been negative for 5 years, DPS held flat at HK$0.40) rather than a compounder. Net cash of HK$1,962m (FY2025), risen to HK$6,231m by H1-2026, is added in the equity bridge.
scenario_narratives.bull: The investment-portfolio unwind stabilises quickly and a broadening Hong Kong luxury-residential recovery (>HK$100m transaction volumes +156% YoY in Q1 2026, rate cuts, improving equity markets) drives faster Peak Portfolio and Kai Tak sales recognition than the base case, the Mainland DP legacy book finishes working through its impairments sooner, Changsha/Chengdu IFS keep attracting flagship luxury-brand expansions, and Modern Terminals' DaChan Bay diversification offsets more of the Hong Kong port decline. UNP grows mid-single-digit for several years before fading to a still-modest terminal rate.
scenario_narratives.bear: A renewed Mainland China property downturn or Hong Kong rate/policy shock repeats the FY2022 pattern (UNP fell to just HK$303m that year): the portfolio unwind is forced at weaker prices, Mainland office oversupply deepens and IP profit falls rather than holds, fresh DP impairments reappear, China's tighter outbound-investment rules and Hong Kong's higher ultra-luxury stamp duty specifically cool the Peak Portfolio's core buyer pool, and Modern Terminals' Hong Kong throughput decline continues unmitigated. UNP falls sharply for two years before stabilising at a low terminal growth rate; the net-cash balance sheet means this is an earnings and multiple case, not a solvency case.

valuation_philosophy.summary: 0004.HK is valued on Underlying Net Profit -- the company's own audited, consistently-defined non-GAAP measure that strips non-cash Mainland investment-property revaluation swings and mark-to-market movements on financial instruments -- capitalised at the HKD cost of equity, because UNP is already a post-interest, post-tax, attributable distributable-earnings flow (net debt is therefore held at zero and the Group's actual net cash, HK$1,962m at FY2025 year-end, is added separately in the equity bridge). Statutory net income (HK$50m profit FY2025, HK$3,224m LOSS FY2024) is unusable for a growth DCF: it swings on IP revaluation deficits of HK$3.6-6.0bn/year that have nothing to do with the cash economics of the underlying malls, hotels, development pipeline and container terminals. Statutory revenue is likewise not a coherent growth base -- it nearly halved FY2021-FY2025 purely because the Group deliberately stopped buying Mainland DP land in 2019 and progressively realised ~HK$9.7bn of its investment portfolio in FY2025 alone, while UNP itself held up. The single biggest judgement in this model is the near-term UNP path: the FY2025 base of HK$4,104m already reflects a materially larger Investments-segment (dividend income) contribution than the run-rate management has since disclosed for H1-2026 (UNP down 17% YoY, Investments profit down 41%), so the base case explicitly steps UNP down for one to two years before letting the shrinking DP-impairment drag and resilient core property/logistics businesses stabilise growth at a low single-digit rate consistent with 5 years of essentially flat-to-declining NAV per share and a flat HK$0.40/share dividend.
key_risks_to_valuation: The Investments-portfolio unwind path is the largest single swing factor: if dividend income from the remaining ~HK$40bn book falls faster than modelled (forced realisation at weak prices), UNP falls further than the base case; if the unwind pauses and the retained portfolio recovers with markets, UNP holds up better than modelled.

Mainland China office oversupply and the DP legacy-book impairment cadence are largely outside management's control and could either fade faster (bull) or reappear in size (bear, as they did in FY2022 and FY2024).

The Hong Kong ultra-luxury segment (Peak Portfolio) that the growth path leans on for its DP recovery is directly exposed to both the February 2026 stamp-duty hike and China's July 2026 outbound-investment regulation, both aimed at exactly this buyer pool.

Discount rate: the terminal value is a meaningful share of the base case (Gordon-growth terminal on a 9.5% cost of equity and 2.0% terminal growth); each 1pp on the cost of equity moves the base value materially.

This is a UNP-capitalisation model, not a NAV/asset-based model: book NAV/share (HK$48.01 FY2025) sits well above the DCF's per-share output, reflecting the market's persistent discount to book for this conglomerate structure (Wheelock control ~68-71%, complex cross-holdings with sister company Wharf REIC) rather than a modelling error -- a sum-of-parts/NAV cross-check would likely value the Group higher than the earnings-capitalisation approach used here, and is worth running as a memo if the discount to NAV becomes the live investment question.

0004.HK straddles the REIT-adjacent row (IP fair-value swings, capitalise post-financing flow) and the holdco/mixed-conglomerate row (DP, hotels, logistics, investment portfolio) rather than fitting either cleanly; a future update could instead sum-of-parts the segments (IP at a cap rate, DP/hotels/logistics at earnings multiples, investment portfolio at fair value) rather than capitalising the single blended UNP line, which would separate the true property-yield economics from the highly variable Investments-segment contribution.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance v8 chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 17.68-30.60 HKD
data_sources.financials: 0004.HK_Metrics.csv / core_metrics and kpis (FY2017-FY2025, H1 FY2022-FY2026); 0004.HK_Annual_FY2025.txt Financial Highlights (p.5, lines ~200-232), Financial Review UNP/segment discussion (lines 960-1000), Ten-Year Financial Summary (lines 8440-8560); 0004.HK_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt Financial Review (lines 140-180), net cash disclosure (lines 336-345)
data_sources.qualitative: 0004.HK_Analysis.json (2026-09-26); FY2025 Annual Report Chairman's Statement and H1-2026 Interim Report outlook sections

inputs.base_revenue_basis: FY2025 Underlying Net Profit (UNP) of HK$4,104m used AS the flow base, not statutory revenue. Statutory revenue (HK$10,997m FY2025, down from HK$22,378m FY2021) is not a usable growth anchor here: it is falling for structural, non-distress reasons (Mainland DP land bank deliberately unbought since 2019 and being sold down; Investments portfolio ~HK$9.7bn realised in FY2025 alone) while UNP margin on revenue mechanically rises as a result (16.3% FY2021 -> 37.3% FY2025), so revenue x margin is not a coherent build for this business. UNP is projected directly: `ebitda_margin_path` is held at 100% (base_revenue IS the flow) and growth_rates apply directly to UNP.
inputs.share_count_basis: 3,056m shares in issue, flat since FY2021 (Annual Report 5yr summary and H1-2026 interim, weighted average 3,056m both periods). No buybacks, no material share-based payments (SBC-zero market).
inputs.net_debt_note: Deliberately ZERO in the model. UNP is stated 'primarily excluding' revaluation and MTM items but IS already after net finance costs (FY2025 finance costs before capitalisation HK$448m, net of interest income HK$279m) and after tax and NCI. Deducting the balance-sheet net cash/debt figure on top of a post-financing flow would double count financing (dcf-methods SKILL.md: never subtract net debt from an already-post-interest flow). The Group's actual FY2025 year-end position is net CASH of HK$1,962m (H1-2026: HK$6,231m), added in the equity bridge below rather than left in net_debt so it does not distort the discount-rate mechanics. total_debt/cash recorded for audit only.
inputs.last_fcf_note: = FY2025 Underlying Net Profit, treated as the distributable owner flow (see base_revenue_basis). No further SBC/interest adjustment: SBC is nil (0004.HK is an SBC-zero market per owner-fcf-adaptations.md section (e)) and interest income is already inside UNP.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: Statutory profit attributable to shareholders, FY2025 (HK$50m), included for audit only. It is NOT used anywhere in the projection: it is dominated by a HK$3,641m attributable IP revaluation deficit, an HK$803m MTM/exchange loss on financial instruments and a HK$205m hotel impairment, none of which are cash or recurring in the sense a DCF should project. FY2024 statutory profit was a HK$3,224m LOSS on a HK$5,990m revaluation deficit despite UNP of HK$2,798m that year -- statutory net income has no usable trend for this business.
inputs.sbc_source: No stock-based compensation disclosed in any FY2018-FY2025 cash flow statement or equity-award footnote (SBC-zero market, HKEX conglomerate). House and street bases coincide; band_position set to null.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2025 interest received HK$279m sits inside UNP (nets within the Investments segment/finance-costs line) and is not stripped separately, because net_debt/cash is not deducted from the flow (excluded-income/matching-asset rule satisfied in the other direction, as with CHC.AX/GMG.AX).
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-25T08:08:12Z Yahoo Finance v8 chart meta (HKEX regular close); 52-week range 17.68-30.60 HKD
inputs.balance_sheet_date: 2025-12-31 (FY2025 annual); H1-2026 interim balance sheet dated 2026-06-30 shows net cash risen further to HK$6,231m, referenced as corroborating trend evidence only -- FY2025 year-end remains the modelled anchor since it is the last completed annual balance sheet
inputs.wacc_rationale: HKD cost of equity (not a WACC): flow is post-interest and post-tax, no net debt deducted. HKD risk-free approximated via the USD peg (~4.0-4.3% UST 10yr, Sept 2026) plus a Hong Kong/China property equity risk premium of ~5.0-5.5pp reflecting Mainland office oversupply and cyclicality (Analysis.json rates Mainland macro risk 'high'), less a modest discount for the scale/diversification and net-cash balance sheet: 9.5% flat across scenarios. Risk (cyclicality, Mainland concentration, conglomerate-structure discount) is charged in the flows and probability weights per owner-fcf-adaptations.md (f), not stacked again as a WACC premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not material: 0004.HK's own operating properties/offices carry lease liabilities of only HK$3m (FY2025 annual report note), immaterial against a HK$146.7bn equity base. No lease adjustment applied.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are attributable-only by construction: 'Underlying net profit' and its segment components (IP 2,197 / DP -478 / Logistics 403 / Investments 1,763 FY2025) are all stated attributable to Wharf Holdings shareholders after minority interests in JVs (e.g. Mount Nicholson 50%, Victoria Voyage 30%, HK Air Cargo Terminals 21%) and consolidated subsidiaries (Modern Terminals NCI). No further NCI deduction in the bridge.
inputs.tax_note: No separate cash_tax_rate applied in the engine (set to 0%): UNP is already stated after the Group's actual income tax charge/credit (FY2025: net tax CREDIT of HK$78m on reversal of Mainland deferred tax provisions; FY2024: HK$3,705m charge, mostly non-cash deferred tax tied to the same IP revaluations already excluded from UNP). Re-applying a tax rate on top of an already-after-tax measure would double-tax the flow.
inputs.engine_mapping: base_revenue = UNP itself (HK$4,104m FY2025). ebitda_margin_path = 100% for all years (the 'revenue' IS the flow, so ebitda = revenue by construction). da_pct_path and capex_pct_path are both held near-zero (D&A and reinvestment capex are already netted off in arriving at UNP as a bottom-line segment-profit measure -- committed development/reinvestment capex of ~HK$15bn is funded from the net-cash balance sheet and portfolio realisation proceeds already reflected in the equity bridge, not as a recurring drag on the distributable earnings stream). cash_tax_rate_path = 0% (see tax_note). growth_rates therefore drive UNP directly year-on-year and fcf out of the engine converges to (projected UNP) with a small deduction/addition only from the residual da/capex wedge (kept at 0 to leave UNP as the clean output).
inputs.notes: MODEL CHOICE: 0004.HK is a diversified conglomerate (Mainland investment-property malls/offices + HK/Mainland for-sale development + hotels + container-terminal logistics + a large, deliberately-shrinking marked-to-market investment portfolio) whose statutory net income has been near-breakeven or negative in 3 of the last 4 years (FY2022 -1,705; FY2024 -3,224; FY2025 +50) purely because of non-cash Mainland IP revaluation deficits (HK$3,641m FY2025, HK$5,990m FY2024) and MTM swings on financial instruments -- textbook 'fair-value movements are not earnings' per dcf-methods SKILL.md. A standard owner-FCF DCF on statutory net income/FCF would be meaningless (reported FCF swings with working capital/DP inventory timing, not operating economics). The company itself publishes and consistently defines a non-GAAP 'Underlying Net Profit' every period since at least FY2017 (excludes IP revaluation, MTM on financial instruments, and other non-cash items) and targets a dividend payout of ~30% of UNP -- this is a clean, audited, company-defined distributable-earnings series, directly analogous to Charter Hall's 'Operating Earnings' and Goodman's 'Operating Profit'. UNP is capitalised at the HKD cost of equity with net_debt held at zero because UNP is already post-interest and post-tax; the Group's actual net cash (HK$1,962m FY2025, up to HK$6,231m by H1-2026 mid-year) is added back explicitly in the equity bridge below instead. REVENUE CAVEAT: statutory revenue nearly halved FY2021->FY2025 (22,378 -> 10,997) almost entirely from the deliberate Mainland DP land-bank wind-down (no land bought since 2019) and the progressive realisation of the ~HK$40-43bn investment portfolio, NOT from a shrinking underlying business -- ex-Investments, H1-2026 revenue and profit both grew (+2%/+6% per company disclosure), so revenue is not used as the growth base (see base_revenue_basis/engine_mapping). BASE-YEAR CAUTION: the disclosed H1-2026 UNP fell 17% YoY to HK$1,697m (H1-2025: HK$2,035m), driven by Investments segment profit falling 41% as the portfolio continues to be unwound (dividend income shrinking on a smaller book), partly offset by higher interest income (net cash growing) and better HK DP sales recognition. The FY2025 full-year UNP of HK$4,104m therefore still contains a fuller-sized Investments contribution than the run-rate going into FY2026-27; the base-case near-term growth path below explicitly steps UNP down in Y1-Y2 to reflect the further portfolio unwind already disclosed, before flattening/recovering modestly as the shrinking DP drag fades and IP/Logistics hold. NAV context: book value/NAV-per-share fell 5yr CAGR -2.4% (HK$53.02 FY2021 -> HK$48.01 FY2025) and DPS has been held flat at HK$0.40/share throughout (payout ratio swinging 30-400%+ of UNP in low years) -- this is a mature, capital-return conglomerate, not a growth story, consistent with the low terminal growth used below. FY0 for growth path purposes is FY2025 UNP (4,104); the H1-2026 print is treated as corroborating evidence for the Y1 step-down rather than restated as a new FY0 anchor, since it is only a half-year.

bear.growth_rationale: A renewed Mainland China property downturn and/or Hong Kong rate/stamp-duty shock repeats or worsens the FY2022 pattern (UNP collapsed to HK$303m that year): the Investments portfolio unwind accelerates or is forced at weaker prices (dividend income falls faster than the base case), Mainland office oversupply deepens (severity already rated 'high' in Analysis.json) pushing IP profit down rather than flat, fresh Mainland DP impairment provisions reappear on the remaining inventory, China's tighter Outbound Investment Regulation (effective July 2026) and the February 2026 HK stamp-duty hike on >HK$100m transactions materially cool the Peak Portfolio's highest-value buyer pool, and Modern Terminals' Hong Kong throughput decline (-6% FY2025, -6% H1-2026) continues unmitigated by DaChan Bay growth. UNP falls sharply for two years before stabilising at a low, low-single-digit terminal growth -- no solvency question arises given the net-cash balance sheet (this is an earnings/multiple case, not a survival case).

base.growth_rationale: Y1 (-8%) and Y2 (-4%): the disclosed H1-2026 UNP run-rate (-17% YoY) reflects a further step-down in Investments segment profit (-41% H1-2026) as the ~HK$40bn portfolio continues to be progressively realised; full-year FY2026 is modelled softer than FY2025's HK$4,104m base but not as sharply down as the H1 print alone, since higher interest income on the growing net-cash pile and improving HK DP sales recognition (Kai Tak/Peak) partly offset it, and FY2027 sees a further smaller step down as the portfolio unwind continues. From Y3 the drag fades: DP loss continues to narrow (down 75% in FY2025 alone as the legacy Mainland book is worked through) and IP/Logistics hold roughly flat to modestly positive, supporting a return to low-single-digit growth by Y3-Y4, tapering to the 2.0% terminal reflecting a mature, capital-return conglomerate (NAV/share CAGR has been negative over the past 5 years) rather than a growth compounder.
base.margin_rationale: Fixed at 100%: the projected 'revenue' series IS Underlying Net Profit by construction (see engine_mapping), so ebitda = revenue in every year and no further margin judgement is layered on top.

bull.growth_rationale: The investment-portfolio unwind stabilises sooner (a smaller, higher-quality residual book still throws off resilient dividend income) while the Hong Kong residential recovery broadens further than the base case: luxury transaction volumes keep climbing (already +156% YoY in Q1 2026 for >HK$100m deals) so Peak Portfolio (Mount Nicholson, Plantation Road) and Kai Tak/Kowloon Tong (Victoria Voyage, Monet) sales recognition accelerates, the Mainland DP legacy book finishes working through its impairments faster than management guides, Changsha/Chengdu IFS continue attracting luxury-brand expansion even as broader Mainland retail struggles, and Modern Terminals' DaChan Bay growth (+16% H1-2026) offsets more of the Hong Kong throughput decline. UNP grows mid-single-digit for several years before fading to a still-modest 2.5% terminal (the group remains a mature capital-return conglomerate even in the bull case).

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear lifted above the house default of 15-25% to 30%: Analysis.json rates Mainland China office oversupply, Mainland DP impairments and the Mainland macro/property downturn all 'high' severity, a FY2022-style UNP collapse (to HK$303m, a 93% one-year fall) has occurred within the trailing 5 years, and the H1-2026 print already shows a 17% YoY UNP decline in train before any fresh shock. Bull held at 25%: it requires several things to go right simultaneously (portfolio unwind stabilising, broadening HK luxury recovery continuing despite the February 2026 stamp-duty hike and July 2026 outbound-investment rules, Mainland DP impairments fading on schedule, logistics diversification outrunning HK port decline). Base at 45% (below the house 50% default) to reflect that the current trajectory (H1-2026 already down double-digits) makes the flat-to-modest-growth base case itself somewhat optimistic relative to the disclosed run-rate, without fully weighting the deeper bear case.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
